title: One agent — what it is, what stops it, and what it can build a trade on

data.name: agent
data.shape: Agent — displayName, status, revision, binding, brain, modelDisplayName, tradingConfig, performance, permissions
data.source: app.listAgents.execute, the row matching the route id

data.name: radar
data.shape: ReadDeploymentsResult ('deployed' | 'not-deployed' | unreadable) — per deployment: coinTicker, timeframe, standing, occupancy
data.source: app.readDeployments.execute — takes the whole agent and the rest of the roster, because standing needs the lifecycle and occupancy needs everyone else's

data.name: exposure
data.shape: { exposure, fills } — money at stake right now

data.name: feasibility
data.shape: FeasibilityReply | null — { agentId, issuedAt, advisory: { dials, counts, coins[] }, coinsCarried }. `coins[]` is a two-arm union: priced (band, requested, blocking dial, shortfall) or unpriced (ticker only, no numbers).
data.source: app.readFeasibilityReply.execute — NOT a platform read. `update_intelligence_agent` returns the advisory beside the agent and no read tool answers it, so this collects the signed reply the edit action set down a redirect ago. null on absent, tampered, another agent's, or older than 120s.

components.purpose: Read one agent: how it has done, what it can trade on right now, what money is at stake, what keeps stopping it, what it inherits, where it is deployed, and what may be done to it.
components.current_implementation: max-w-3xl centered column, space-y-6, p-6. Order is deliberate and argued in the source: record, then feasibility, then exposure (money at stake now, above everything retrospective), then stoppages (the answer to every other question on the page), then binding, owned fields, deployment, actions. `roster-unreadable` and `no-such-agent` are max-w-2xl short pages. The page reads no `?problem=` — the rename form that minted one moved to /agents/[id]/edit, and an unreachable branch was removed rather than restyled. The brain line is inline in the page rather than a component: it prefers the platform's own modelDisplayName and falls back to the preset name or the model id, never to an invented one.
constraints: Each read renders independently and one failing hides none of the others — an unreadable radar must never render as 'not deployed', and an unreadable stoppage history must never render as an agent nothing has stopped

This route holds no bound form. It stopped being a mutation route when the rename moved to /agents/[id]/edit, and `only-mcp-control`'s corridor guard depends on that; a design must not reintroduce a form here
Every state change is a full navigation. No client state, no optimistic rendering, no partial update

The inline brain line must never invent a name the platform did not report — the read-back flattens the request's two-branch brain union into one field, so it cannot say whether a brain is a preset or a named model, and the line claims neither

components.purpose: Turn BattleGrid's per-coin stop bands into the sentence an operator reads: how many of this agent's armed coins its strategy can build a stop for at today's volatility, which dial is stopping the rest, and which way the ceiling costs them.
components.current_implementation:
A section with an h2 and a stack of

at space-y-2 — prose, no table, no chart. `absent` is the default and renders NOTHING at all: the platform answers feasibility on a write and never on a read, so an ordinary page load has no answer to show. `says-nothing` (an advisory over zero armed coins) also renders nothing. The headline pairs BattleGrid's own counts.buildable/counts.total with counts.evaluated. Blocked coins are grouped by responsible dial into one sentence, with an unattributed group of its own. Unpriced coins get a separate sentence naming them. The ceiling curve is up to three candidate ceilings read off the returned bands, highest first, followed by a text-text-secondary line marking it as this product's arithmetic. `counts-disagree` and `coins-not-carried` are role=status lines. A provenance line closes the panel. Every sentence with an interpolation is a single template literal.
constraints: The platform's counts and this product's ceiling curve are DIFFERENT CLAIMS and must stay visually and verbally distinguishable. A design that unifies them into one figure group, one stat row, or one chart is requires-spec-change (spec: A Ceiling Is Shown Against The Opportunity It Costs — 'SHALL be presented as derived rather than as a platform claim')

An unpriced coin is never rendered among the blocked. It is a gap in the reading, not a verdict on the coin, and the two must not share a group, a colour, or a count (spec: A Coin Whose Volatility Could Not Be Read)

`absent` renders nothing — not an empty state, not a placeholder, not a zero. A design that gives this panel a resting appearance would put a permanent frame around an answer that exists for two minutes after an edit and never otherwise, and 'no advisory' must never read as 'no coin can construct' (spec: The Platform Returns No Advisory)

The provenance line and the dial-direction line are load-bearing copy, not chrome. Without provenance the figures read as a standing property of the agent rather than one moment's reading of live volatility; without the direction line an operator cannot learn that only a LOWER ceiling costs opportunity. Neither may be moved behind a disclosure, a tooltip, or a hover
No sorting, ranking, or emphasis that implies one coin is a better trade than another. This panel says what can be constructed, never what should be
Copy may not be re-split into JSX fragments around interpolations — the rendering harness joins adjacent text nodes with a space and the tests assert whole sentences

components.purpose: How the agent has done, from the performance block the roster payload already carried.
components.current_implementation: Rendered only when agent.performance is non-null. An agent that has played nothing reports a record full of zeroes and says so in its own words, so the component never sees a null.
constraints: A record of zeroes is a real record and must not be styled as an empty state

components.purpose: Money at stake right now — open positions, their fills, and the stop that stands.
components.current_implementation: Own component with its own WhyNotLoaded branch. Sits above everything retrospective on this page.
constraints: Stays above the backward-looking sections: an agent can be holding a leveraged position with a moved stop, and that is the one fact on this page that is about now

components.purpose: What keeps stopping this agent, before anything about how it is configured.
components.current_implementation: Three arms rendered distinctly; the unreadable arm is a role=status paragraph carrying the reason.
constraints: A history that could not be read must never dress up as an agent nothing has stopped

components.purpose: State the agent's strategy binding as BattleGrid reports it.
components.current_implementation:
One

inside the 'Its strategy binding' section (h2 + two

).
constraints: The binding state is BattleGrid's word for it and is not re-derived here

components.purpose: Say what the agent inherits from the strategy it is bound to — where inheritance is true at all.
components.current_implementation:
The second

of the binding section. Its own component because the heading once read 'Inherited from its strategy' over a sentence asserted for every binding, including an ORPHANED one whose strategy cannot be read.
constraints: The inheritance claim must not be asserted for an ORPHANED binding — there is no strategy to inherit from, and saying otherwise is a false statement about where the agent's rules come from

components.purpose: Say whether this agent's money limits are actually set — not merely that a configuration object exists.
components.current_implementation:
One

inside the 'Owned by the agent' section, beside the inline brain line.
constraints: A present tradingConfig object is not a set limit. The live account's active agent carries a full twenty-field config in which two of three caps are zero, which BattleGrid reads as no cap — a design must not render 'configured' as a satisfied state

components.purpose: Whether this agent is actually doing anything — the fact its lifecycle status hides.
components.current_implementation: A <ul> of deployments, each a standing sentence plus an optional occupancy sentence plus an Undeploy link; then a Deploy link. Keyed by `${coinTicker}-${timeframe}`.
constraints: ACTIVE means configured; only a radar deployment means scanning. A design must not merge the lifecycle badge and the deployment standing into one indicator
'Deployed and unscanned' is a distinct fact from 'on duty' and must remain readable as one
An unreadable radar must never dress up as 'not deployed'

components.purpose: What may be done to this agent — each a link to its own confirmation route.
components.current_implementation: Links only. No bound form on this route.
constraints: Every one is a navigation to a route that states the consequence and issues a confirmation. A design must not turn any of them into an in-place control that acts on press

flows.name: Edit an agent and learn what it can still trade
steps: follow Edit to /agents/[id]/edit, type the change, review the stated consequence
apply — the action performs the write and sets down BattleGrid's feasibility reply
land back on /agents/[id], where the feasibility panel states how many armed coins can construct and which dial holds the rest
the panel stops rendering two minutes later; editing again is what asks anew

flows.name: Read one agent
steps: read the record, then money at stake now, then what keeps stopping it
read the binding and what it inherits
read whether it is deployed and scanning, which its ACTIVE status does not say

accessibility.notes: The feasibility panel is display-only and takes no focus. Its two conditional caveats — the counts disagreement and the not-carried notice — are role=status, not role=alert: neither is a failure, and both describe the reading rather than interrupting it. Failed reads elsewhere on the page carry role=status with the reason. The panel's absence is silent by design, so no live region announces it.
